parsed.explanation: One national statute book; no subnational variation. No trans-specific criminal offence, no documented police targeting of trans people, no documented border or custody practice, and no hate-crime data. The operative negative is a latent colonial male-same-sex felony that can reach a trans woman read as male; enforcement was undocumented as of 2013 and the present is unresolved. There is no gender-identity protection or traveller-facing remedy. Traditional social discrimination is noted, but no government abuses. UN SOGI statements and an HIV programme including transgender residents signal institutional awareness, not visitor protection. Thin data and open questions keep the score below documented acceptance-with-protections jurisdictions but above states with documented targeting or universal exclusion.

entry_documents.exposure: No source covers entry, visa or border-screening treatment of trans travellers; no documented document-mismatch practice.
entry_documents.interaction: Border stage is an open question; absence of documented friction cannot be treated as safety.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Sections 153–155 create felony exposure for male homosexual conduct; a trans woman read as male could fall within scope. No custody-treatment findings.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No trans-specific custody protocol or remedy documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Charge and custody classification depend on officers' reading, not identity; enforcement after 2013 is unresolved.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No documented facility-access, ward-placement or custody-placement rule for trans visitors.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Small single statute book; no subnational variation documented, but no facility practice recorded.

care_services.exposure: No visitor care-access denial documented; HIV response includes transgender residents but not traveller care.
care_services.protection: No gender-identity protection in health or services documented.
care_services.interaction: Institutional awareness of key populations exists, but no operative traveller-facing safeguard is shown.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: No trans-specific criminalisation or official threat-framing documented; male-same-sex felony remains on the books.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: No gender-identity anti-discrimination or hate-crime provision documented; no government abuses reported in 2013.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Latent statute plus absent enforcement data creates uncertainty, not documented targeting.

minors_guardians.exposure: No education, youth-service or trans-minor findings; age-of-consent asymmetry documented for male same-sex conduct.
minors_guardians.interaction: Adult travelling with a minor faces no documented trans-specific rule, but the stage is unevidenced.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No hate-crime incidents, statistics or trans-specific violence documented; traditional customs noted as socially discriminatory.
street_violence_police_response.protection: No hate-crime legislation or police-response record documented.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Social discrimination is recorded, but no pattern of street targeting or official complicity is shown.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No trans-specific complaint mechanism or remedy documented; enforcement data stops at 2013.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Open questions about present enforcement, border practice and custody cannot be resolved from the dossier.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.55-B documents border secondary screening, refused admission and slow remedies. This dossier documents no such border practice, so exposure is less evidenced; but it has a latent felony and no documented remedy, so the two sit in a similar uncertain range.

0.65-A has a documented stop and intrusive questioning, but national equality law and a working complaint remedy. This dossier has no documented incident but also no operative protection, so it is placed below that documented-remedy tier.

0.75-C has trained border officers, tribunal appeals and brief detention with compensation. This dossier lacks documented border training or enforceable remedy, so it scores materially lower despite no recorded violence.
0.45-D imposes universal address registration and nightly hotel reporting. This dossier documents no such universal exposure, so it sits above 0.45-D despite the unresolved sodomy-law risk.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime is one national system with no documented subnational variation. The strongest documented negative is the latent male-same-sex felony, which can reach a trans woman who is read as male; enforcement was absent as of 2013 and is not documented afterwards. There is no gender-identity protection, hate-crime record, border, custody or facility data. Traditional social discrimination is noted, but no government abuses or organised targeting. Institutional awareness through HIV programming and UN SOGI statements is a climate signal only. The result is a thin-data jurisdiction with serious unresolved possibilities but no documented traveller-facing campaign, placing it in the lower Reduced Risk band.
